messages:
katie_support: Customer on private VPC (acct: acme-payments) reporting intermittent RSTs on streaming inference when sending large batched requests. Happens only from their app subnet, not from a test host in same VPC.

ryan_eng: Can you paste the client curl / grpc call and which port they're using?

katie_support: Using our streaming API over TLS to port 443, request pattern is ~500 tokens in a single streamed response. They see a chunk of tokens then RST from their side. No 4xx/5xx from our side.

maria_netops: Any chance of a middlebox rewriting ephemeral source ports? VPC NAT or on-prem firewall with port-mapping can cause return-path mismatch.

katie_support: Customer says they have a stateful firewall that does SNAT at the on-prem edge. They ran tcpdump and captured server -> client SYN-ACK then client RST. Provided a pcap excerpt attached.

alex_sre: Quick check: are we reusing the same backend connection for multiplexed streams? If they SNAT different flows to same source port, conntrack state could be confused.

ryan_eng: We do keep long-lived TLS connection with HTTP/2 streams. We rely on TCP 5-tuple for stateful routing. If SNAT rewrites source port mid-stream it will break.

katie_support: Customer ran: `sudo tcpdump -n host 10.11.12.13 and port 443 -w out.pcap` and saw server packets to client IP X.Y.Z.W:49152 then client replied from X.Y.Z.W:49153 with RST.

maria_netops: That is classic ephemeral port shadowing. The on-prem firewall is load-balancing/masquerading multiple internal clients to the same external IP but different source ports and sometimes rewriting ports on return. Need to confirm NACL/SG on their VPC too.

customer_jira: +1 we have an F5 in front that does SNAT pools. We thought it was transparent. We'll check SNAT automap settings.

ryan_eng: For repro, can we get cc of their fw rules or a packet capture from the NAT device showing mapping table? Also a minimal curl test to stream with `--no-buffer` to reproduce easily.

katie_support: Asked for NAT dump. Meanwhile I ran a quick test from our side: `openssl s_client -connect client-ip:443 -quiet` and then sent a long payload and couldn't repro from our public endpoint. Only when traffic originates from their app-subnet.

alex_sre: Suggest they temporarily bypass SNAT (set preserve source on NAT or enable 1:1 mapping) or create a dedicated SNAT port range that is not shared across flows. Also verify their security group doesn't have ephemeral port restrictions that translate to NACL denies.

maria_netops: Another check: NACLs are stateless; if they have deny rules for high ephemeral range on egress, return traffic could be dropped. Ask them to `aws ec2 describe-network-acls` and show the ephemeral range rules.

customer_jira: We found a weird ACL deny: egress port range 49150-49160 DENY from 0.0.0.0/0 (applied during a hardening change). We'll try opening 49150-65535 and retest.

katie_support: Great — please retest streaming after change and send new pcap. Also send the F5 SNAT config.

customer_jira: Changed NACL to allow ephemeral range and disabled F5 SNAT automap for the test (enabled preserve source). Retest shows no RSTs in 20 runs, streaming stable.

ryan_eng: That confirms two issues: (1) NACL blocked some return ephemeral ports causing reset, (2) aggressive SNAT automap caused source-port remapping. We should document recommended network posture for Private customers: allow ephemeral port ranges, avoid SNAT automap for persistent connections, or use 1:1 NAT.

katie_support: Filing KB draft and will include repro steps: tcpdump command, curl/openssl minimal repro, what to check on F5 and NACL rules.

maria_netops: I'll add a short checklist for network onboarding: verify NACL egress 1024-65535 allowed, SG allows established return, and note SNAT behaviors for common appliances.

devops-bot: Incident created: #INC-2026-4192 - private-vpc-ephemeral-port-shadowing. Assigned to netops + support.

katie_support: Closing loop with customer: we'll include KB and recommend config changes. Customer happy and asked for a short note to include with their infra runbook.

alex_sre: marking thread notes: root cause = ephemeral port range partial deny + SNAT automap; mitigation = open ephemeral range or use preserve-source SNAT / 1:1 NAT and ensure stateful devices maintain 5-tuple consistency.

katie_support: Thanks all :raised_hands:
